AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only water vapour

4. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

5. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Milk souring
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Ice melting to water

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying General Crop Harvesting? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on General Crop Harvesting.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to General Crop Harvesting.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for General Crop Harvesting.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about General Crop Harvesting.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of soil? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of soil.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of soil.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of soil.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of soil.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Agricultural Land? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Agricultural Land.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agricultural Land.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Agricultural Land.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Agricultural Land.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Growing Selected Crop? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Growing Selected Crop.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Selected Crop.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Growing Selected Crop.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Growing Selected Crop.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Growing Selected Crops 1.6 Crop Protection: Weed control 1.7 General Crop Harves? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Selected Crops 1.6 Crop Protection: Weed control 1.7 General Crop Harves.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Growing Selected Crops 1.6 Crop Protection: Weed control 1.7 General Crop Harves.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Growing Selected Crops 1.6 Crop Protection: Weed control 1.7 General Crop Harves.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Growing Selected Crops 1.6 Crop Protection: Weed control 1.7 General Crop Harves.

11. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Heating until a solid melts

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Protection: Weed control? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Protection: Weed control.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Protection: Weed control.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Protection: Weed control.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Protection: Weed control.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain General Animal Health and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Beekeeping and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Animal Rearing Project 3.0 Agricultural Technologies and Entrepreneurship 3.1 To and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Animal Rearing Project and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

2. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. C — Glucose and oxygen

4. C — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

5. D — Ice melting to water

6. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for General Crop Harvesting.

7. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of soil.

8. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agricultural Land.

9. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Selected Crop.

10. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Selected Crops 1.6 Crop Protection: Weed control 1.7 General Crop Harves.

11. A — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

12. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Protection: Weed control.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Beekeeping; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Animal Rearing Project 3.0 Agricultural Technologies and Entrepreneurship 3.1 To; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Animal Rearing Project; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
